title: What a packet narrative is meant to say, beside a case whose identifiers could be read into it: amounts, dates (a year, a month and day, or a month's name that is a number or a name of the case), codes, units, an NPI, a plan identifier the facts hold, another person's Social Security- or phone-shaped number, citation markers, identifier placeholders and fact tokens that spell an identifier, a label, a placeholder and then a date, and the words that are a short part of a hyphenated name ("in" beside HYE-IN, "to" beside TO-UYEN); generated narratives of such pieces and of written identifiers; the browser's check
assertion: None of it is read as an identifier, and the code's own draft passes for any case whose identifiers it does not hold; the verifier flags an identifier wherever its whole-word reading or the gateway's narrative matcher (`nameOrNumberMatches`, the reading the drafter's check of its facts starts from) holds one outside the tokens and the dated figures, but for a part of a name's word under four letters by itself, and nowhere that neither they nor the reading across a token do; the drafter's check (`holdsNameOrNumber`) holds wherever the reading the verifier asks where (`nameOrNumberMatches`) finds a match, on any text in its NFKC form that holds none of the gateway's own placeholders (the check normalizes and masks for itself), and answers as that reading does on a text that holds none of the forms the check alone reads (MOD-25: a number as the records hold it, a piece of it, digits glued to a letter, a word of a name held with a mark); leaving an identifier out changes no other's matches; the browser's check loads neither the matcher nor the server's reading
noFileReason: Narratives are generated in memory by the property test from pieces it holds; no file.
